definition_en: to stay until something happens, to be left until later, to serve someone, or a period of waiting
core_image: 公交站上，男孩看着手表等下一班车
scene: 公交站上，男孩看着手表等下一班车 At the bus stop the boy keeps looking at his watch and waits for the next bus.
sceneCN: 这里 wait 是「等待」（第 01 个义项）；句意是在这里等公交车。

senses.title: To stay until something happens
senses.definition: To stay until something happens
senses.example: Wait here for the bus.
senses.why: From Old French waitier, to watch, the verb first meant staying on guard.
senses.whyCN: 经古法语 waitier（看守），动词最初指守候。

senses.title: To be left until later
senses.definition: To be left until later
senses.example: The work can wait.
senses.why: What is left standing is put off, so waiting also means delay.
senses.whyCN: 被搁着不动，便引申为往后推。

senses.title: To serve someone
senses.definition: To serve someone
senses.example: She waits on customers at the shop.
senses.why: Standing ready to serve gave the verb its sense of attending.
senses.whyCN: 站在一旁随时照应，便生出伺候之义。

senses.title: A period of waiting
senses.definition: A period of waiting
senses.example: There was a long wait at the station.
senses.why: The verb turned into a noun for the stretch of time spent waiting.
senses.whyCN: 动词转作名词，指等候所花的一段时间。

senses.definition: a large wild animal with thick fur that walks on flat feet

senses.example: A bear left deep prints across the snow.
senses.exampleCN: 一只熊在雪地上留下深深的脚印。
senses.why: The noun bear goes back to Old English bera, 'the brown one', a name that replaced the animal's true name to avoid saying it aloud.
senses.whyCN: 名词 bear 来自古英语 bera「棕色的那个」，日耳曼人用颜色代称这种猛兽，以免直呼其名。

senses.title: To carry a heavy thing
senses.definition: to carry something heavy, or to hold weight
senses.definitionCN: 承担重量，或把重物带着走
senses.example: She bore the heavy box upstairs.
senses.exampleCN: 她把沉重的箱子里搬上了楼。
senses.why: The verb bear comes from Old English beran, 'to carry', and its oldest work is carrying a load on the body.
senses.whyCN: 动词 bear 来自古英语 beran「携带」，最古老的任务就是用身体扛着东西走。

senses.title: To endure something hard
senses.definition: to suffer or accept something difficult without giving way
senses.definitionCN: 艰难之事压在身上而不垮掉
senses.example: I can't bear the noise.
senses.why: If a body can carry a heavy load, it can also carry pain or noise; 'carrying' becomes 'enduring'.
senses.whyCN: 身体扛得住重物，也就能扛住疼痛和噪音；「承载」于是变成「忍受」。

senses.title: To give birth to a child
senses.definition: to give birth to a child
senses.example: She bore a son in the spring.
senses.exampleCN: 她在春天生下了一个儿子。
senses.why: A mother carries the child inside her before birth, so the 'carrying' verb naturally came to mean giving birth.
senses.whyCN: 母亲在生出孩子之前先把他带在身上，所以这个「承载」的动词自然引申为生育。

senses.title: To show or have a mark or name
senses.definition: to have a mark, name or sign on it
senses.definitionCN: 上面带着印记、名字或标志
senses.example: The letter bears no signature.
senses.why: Paper carries ink the way a body carries a load, so bear also means having a mark or name written on something.
senses.whyCN: 纸承载着墨迹，就像身体承载着重物，所以 bear 也表示某物上带着标记或名字。

definition_en: a message sent by computer, or to send such a message

senses.title: An electronic message
senses.definition: a message sent electronically
senses.example: She sent me an email this morning.
senses.exampleCN: 她今天早上给我发了一封电子邮件。
senses.why: The prefix e- stands for electronic, so email is literally an electronic piece of mail, named after the paper mail it replaced.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 e- 是 electronic 的缩写，email 字面就是「电子信件」，沿用了它所取代的纸质邮件的说法。

senses.title: The email service
senses.definition: the service used to send such messages
senses.example: Please contact me by email.
senses.exampleCN: 请通过电子邮件联系我。
senses.why: Once the message had a name, the same word named the channel, just as 'by mail' names a way of sending.
senses.whyCN: 这种信件有了名字之后，同一个词也指传递它的渠道，正如 by mail 指一种寄送方式。

senses.title: To send by email
senses.definition: to send a message electronically
senses.example: I will email you the photos.
senses.exampleCN: 我会把照片发电子邮件给你。
senses.why: English turns communication nouns into verbs (mail, text, phone), and email followed that pattern.
senses.whyCN: 英语常把通信类名词用作动词，如 mail、text、phone，email 也沿用了这一模式。

definition_en: a sweet baked food made from flour, sugar and eggs
core_image: 刚出炉的圆蛋糕摆在桌上，糖霜还没完全凝住
scene: 生日那天，桌上摆着插了蜡烛的圆点心，孩子们围在旁边。 She cut the cake and gave everyone a slice.
sceneCN: 这里 cake 是「甜点蛋糕」（第 01 个义项）；句意是我们为她的生日烤了蛋糕。

derivatives.zh: 由 cake 加 -y 构成，义为「像蛋糕的」
由 cup 与 cake 复合，义为「纸杯蛋糕」

senses.title: A sweet baked food
senses.definition: a sweet food baked from flour, sugar, eggs and fat
senses.definitionCN: 用面粉、糖、蛋和油脂烤成的甜食
senses.example: She baked a cake for my birthday.
senses.exampleCN: 她为我的生日烤了一个蛋糕。
senses.why: Cake comes from Old Norse kaka, a flat baked sweet, and the birthday cake is the sense children know first.
senses.whyCN: cake 来自古诺斯语 kaka，指扁平的甜饼，生日蛋糕就是孩子最先认识的意思。

senses.title: A pressed block of something
senses.definition: a small flat block of a solid substance
senses.example: He bought a cake of soap.
senses.why: Soap, wax and mud are pressed into flat blocks shaped like a cake, so the food name was extended to any such block.
senses.whyCN: 肥皂、蜡和泥被压成扁块，形状像蛋糕，于是这个食物名称扩展到任何这样的块状物。

senses.title: To form a hard crust
senses.definition: to become covered with a hard layer, or to form a hard mass
senses.definitionCN: 表面结成硬层，或凝成硬块
senses.example: The mud caked on his boots.
senses.exampleCN: 泥巴在他的靴子上结成了块。
senses.why: When soft material dries into a crust, it looks like the baked top of a cake, which is the picture behind the verb.
senses.whyCN: 柔软的东西变干结成硬壳时，很像蛋糕烤好的表层，这就是动词背后的画面。

items.en: Cake is probably from Old Norse kaka, a flat baked food.
items.cn: cake 可能来自古诺斯语 kaka，一种扁平的烤制食物。

items.en: Germanic *kakǭ is the reconstructed source, also behind German Kuchen.
items.cn: 日耳曼语 *kakǭ 是重构来源，也与德语 Kuchen 有关。

items.en: The deeper origin is source uncertain; it may be a loan from outside the family.
items.cn: 更早来源不确定；它可能是来自语族之外的借词。

items.en: Middle English cake covered both flat loaves and sweet baked foods.
items.cn: 中古英语 cake 既指扁平面饼，也指甜烤点。

items.en: The word also gives the hard-mass sense and the idiom piece of cake.
items.cn: 这个词还产生「块状物」义与「轻而易举」的习语。

definition_en: a table used for writing or working, or a service counter

scene: 晚自习的教室里，每张桌子前都坐着一个低头写字的人。 She left the letter on his desk.

senses.title: A table for writing or working
senses.definition: a table with a flat top used for writing or working
senses.definitionCN: 供书写或工作的平面桌子
senses.example: She sat at her desk and wrote.
senses.why: Desk came through Italian and Latin from Greek diskos, a flat round plate, and it still names a flat working surface.
senses.whyCN: desk 经意大利语和拉丁语来自希腊语 diskos「扁平圆盘」，至今仍指扁平的工作台面。

senses.title: A counter where staff serve people
senses.definition: a counter in a hotel, office or shop where staff help visitors
senses.definitionCN: 旅馆、办公室或商店里接待来客的柜台
senses.example: Please ask at the front desk.
senses.why: Hotel and office counters are built like high desks, so the furniture word became the name of the service point.
senses.whyCN: 旅馆和办公室的柜台做得像高书桌，于是家具词变成了服务点的名称。

senses.title: To wish for something
senses.definition: To wish for something
senses.example: I want a glass of water.

senses.whyCN: 源自古诺斯语 vanta（缺少），动词最初指缺什么。

senses.title: To need something
senses.definition: To need something
senses.example: The plant wants more sun.

senses.whyCN: 缺的东西也就是需要的，want 便带上需要之义。

senses.title: To lack something
senses.definition: To lack something
senses.example: He does not want for money.
senses.why: The oldest sense keeps the plain idea of lacking.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项保留了缺少这一本义。

definition_en: the word by which a person or thing is known, or to give such a word to someone
core_image: 手指点在一个写着字的标签上
scene: 新生在教室门口停下，老师低头问他的名字。 The new pupil stopped at the classroom door, and the teacher looked down and asked for his name.
sceneCN: 这里 name 是「名字」（第 1 个义项：人或物的名称）；句意：新生在教室门口停下，老师低头问他的名字。

pos.zh: 给……命名；说出……的名字；任命

senses.title: The word that identifies someone
senses.definition: the word or words by which a person or thing is known and addressed
senses.definitionCN: 用来称呼和辨认某人或某物的词
senses.example: Her name is Lily.
senses.why: A person needs one short label that others can call out, so the word itself becomes the handle of identity.
senses.whyCN: 人需要一个能被别人叫出口的短标签，于是这个词本身成了身份的把手。

senses.title: Reputation or title
senses.definition: the reputation a person or group has, or the title of a thing
senses.definitionCN: 一个人或团体拥有的名声，或事物的名称
senses.example: The company made a name for itself in tea.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司在茶叶上闯出了名声。
senses.why: When people repeat a label often enough, the label carries the group's reputation as well as its identity.
senses.whyCN: 当一个标签被反复提起，它就不仅承载身份，也承载这个团体的名声。

senses.title: To give a name
senses.definition: to give a name to a person, place or thing
senses.definitionCN: 给某人、某地或某物起名字
senses.example: They named the baby after his grandfather.
senses.exampleCN: 他们用祖父的名字给孩子取名。
senses.why: If a name is a handle, the act of naming is handing that handle to someone for the first time.
senses.whyCN: 如果名字是把手，命名就是第一次把这个把手交到某人手里。

senses.title: To say the name or appoint
senses.definition: to state a name openly, or to appoint someone to a position
senses.definitionCN: 公开说出名字，或任命某人担任某职
senses.example: She was named manager last week.
senses.why: Speaking a name in public puts that person forward, and an official announcement turns the act into an appointment.
senses.whyCN: 当众说出一个名字就是把那个人推举出来，正式宣布则使这一动作变成任命。

senses.title: The sister of your father or mother
senses.definition: the sister of one's father or mother
senses.example: My aunt lives across the river.
senses.why: Aunt came into English from Old French ante, from Latin amita, 'father's sister'; English widened it so the mother's sister is also aunt.
senses.whyCN: aunt 从古法语 ante 进入英语，源头是拉丁语 amita「父亲的姐妹」；英语把范围扩大，母亲的姐妹也叫 aunt。

senses.title: The wife of your uncle
senses.definition: the wife of one's uncle
senses.example: Aunt Mary is my uncle's wife.
senses.exampleCN: 玛丽婶婶是我叔叔的妻子。
senses.why: A woman who joins the family by marrying an uncle takes the same title, because the word names a role in the household, not only a blood link.
senses.whyCN: 通过嫁给叔伯舅舅而进入家庭的女性也用同一个称呼，因为这个词标的是家庭里的位置，而不只是血缘。

senses.title: An unrelated older woman close to the family
senses.definition: an unrelated older woman addressed affectionately by a child
senses.definitionCN: 孩子亲昵称呼的、没有血缘关系的年长女性
senses.example: Aunt Li often brings sweets to the children.
senses.exampleCN: 李阿姨常给孩子们带糖。
senses.why: Children extend the family word to friendly older women, so aunt can be a warm form of address with no kinship at all.
senses.whyCN: 孩子把这个家庭称谓扩展到亲近的年长女性，于是 aunt 可以完全没有血缘，只是一种亲切的称呼。

definition_en: a competition in which people try to win
core_image: 舞台上几个孩子轮流朗诵，评委在台下低头打分
scene: 舞台上几个孩子轮流朗诵，评委在台下低头打分。 She enters a singing contest.
sceneCN: 这里 contest 是「比赛」（第 01 个义项）；句意是她报名参加歌唱比赛。

senses.title: A competition with a prize for the winner
senses.definition: an event in which people compete and judges or rules decide who wins
senses.definitionCN: 由评委或规则判定胜负的比拼活动
senses.example: She enters a singing contest.
senses.why: Contest joins con- (together) with a root meaning to witness, so it first pictured people calling each other to witness; a public trial of skill kept that shape.
senses.whyCN: contest 由 con-（一起）加「作证」的词根构成，原本是众人一起对质作证，后来指当众比试高下的活动。

senses.title: To compete for something
senses.definition: to take part in a struggle to win a prize or position
senses.definitionCN: 为奖品或名次参加比拼
senses.example: Three teams contested the cup.
senses.exampleCN: 三支队伍争夺那只奖杯。
senses.why: Turned into a verb, the event word describes what the rivals do inside it: they fight for the same prize.
senses.whyCN: 名词的「比赛」一变成动词，就指参赛者在赛场上做的事：为同一个奖品较量。

senses.title: To argue that something is wrong
senses.definition: to say that a decision or result is not right and try to change it
senses.definitionCN: 认为某个决定或结果不对并设法推翻
senses.example: They contested the referee's decision.
senses.exampleCN: 他们对裁判的判罚提出异议。
senses.why: Two sides calling each other to witness also means standing against each other, and that gave contest the sense of formally disputing a decision.
senses.whyCN: 双方互相传唤作证，也就意味着站到对立面，由此引申出对某个决定正式提出异议。

definition_en: a very short time ago, fair and right, or only
core_image: 钟表的秒针刚跳过整点，门口的人推门进来
scene: 钟表的秒针刚跳过整点，门口的人推门进来。 The bus has just left.
sceneCN: 这里 just 是「刚刚」（第 01 个义项）；句意是公交车刚刚开走。

senses.title: A very short time ago
senses.definition: A very short time ago
senses.example: The bus has just left.
senses.why: Just comes from Latin justus, 'lawful', through French; the time sense grew from 'exactly at that point'.
senses.whyCN: just 经法语来自拉丁语 justus「合法的」；表示时间的义项由「正好在那一点」发展而来。

senses.title: Fair and right
senses.definition: Fair and right
senses.example: The judge made a just decision.
senses.exampleCN: 法官作出了公正的裁决。
senses.why: The oldest sense is legal and moral: something just follows the law and treats people rightly.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项是法律与道德上的：just 的事物合乎法律、公平待人。

senses.title: Only, or exactly
senses.definition: Only, or exactly
senses.example: It costs just five yuan.
senses.why: Because something just reaches a limit and no more, the word came to mean only or exactly.
senses.whyCN: 因为某物正好达到某个界限而不再多，这个词就表示「只」或「正好」。

senses.title: Low in price
senses.definition: costing little money
senses.example: The shoes are cheap in this shop.
senses.why: Cheap goes back to Old English cēap, 'bargain, trade'; a good cheap was a good bargain, and the word narrowed to low price.
senses.whyCN: cheap 来自古英语 cēap「交易、买卖」，good cheap 原指买得划算，后来词义收窄为价钱低。

senses.title: Of low quality
senses.definition: made poorly, so that it does not last or work well
senses.definitionCN: 做得粗糙、不耐用或不好用
senses.example: The chair felt cheap and broke in a week.
senses.exampleCN: 那把椅子一看就廉价，一周就坏了。
senses.why: Things that cost little are often made with poor materials, so cheap also judges the quality of the thing itself.
senses.whyCN: 价钱低的东西常用差材料做成，所以 cheap 也评判东西本身的质量。

senses.title: Mean or unfair
senses.definition: unfair or ungenerous in a way that lowers opinion of someone
senses.definitionCN: 手段低劣或出手小气，让人看不起
senses.example: That was a cheap trick.
senses.why: A person who spends little may also give little in other ways, so cheap came to describe mean behaviour.
